Subject: Novatek redline — choice of law / emergency remedies (MSA)
message_1_body:
Hi Jasmine,

Attached is Novatek's latest redline of the MSA (v3). The primary open points from our side: governing law (Novatek prefers New York), the seat for arbitration (they proposed New York), and a robust carve-out for emergency equitable relief (they want the ability for their local courts to grant TROs and preliminary injunctions without running afoul of an arbitration requirement).

We also included an internal matrix showing which remedies they consider "emergency" vs. "monetary" so you can see the nuance. Two asks from us: 1) Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept New York law? 2) If not, what language would you propose to preserve injunctive relief for the customer while keeping most disputes in arbitration?

We are on an aggressive timeline — procurement would like legal alignment by end of this week so we can move to procurement signature.

Attachments: Novatek_redline_MSA_v3.docx; MSA_emergency_remedies_matrix.xlsx

Thanks,

message_2_headers:

Subject: Re: Novatek redline — choice of law / emergency remedies (MSA)
message_2_body:
Anna —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear matrix. I did a rapid pass with our internal counsel and flagged a couple of pragmatic compromise options so we can close quickly. High level summary:

- Governing law: Redwood prefers Washington state (our HQ). We can accept New York law for the MSA if Novatek requires it for corporate comfort, but we'd like to keep any arbitration seat neutral or tied to the arbitration provider.

- Arbitration vs. injunctive relief: We are comfortable carving injunctive and equitable relief out of arbitration — so either party can seek temporary restraining orders (TROs) or preliminary injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction without waiving arbitration — provided the clause is narrowly tailored.

- Suggested path:
  1) Keep the general dispute resolution (monetary claims) in arbitration (commercial arbitration rules — e.g., AAA/ICC to be confirmed).

  2) Add a clear carve-out sentence: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary or preliminary injunctive or other equitable relief in courts of competent jurisdiction to protect its confidential information or intellectual property, or to prevent irreparable harm."
  3) Add a short venue sentence: "For purposes of such equitable relief only, the parties agree that venue shall be the state and federal courts located in the county where the defendant maintains its principal place of business."

Pros: this preserves arbitration for the bulk of disputes but gives Novatek the practical ability to get emergency relief locally. Cons: it means we accept that a court (possible NY court if defendant is there) can issue injunctive relief independent of arbitration.

Next steps: I want to bring Vivek and Marcus into the thread for the exact clause language we should propose back to Novatek. If you can confirm they need New York governing law specifically (as opposed to simply the "seat"), that will help.

I can also schedule a 20-minute legal-to-legal call today to finalize the redline language; what times work for you?

Best,
Jasmine Liu

message_3_headers:
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Novatek redline — choice of law / emergency remedies (MSA)
message_3_body:
Jasmine / Anna —

Thanks for looping me in. Below is proposed language that balances enforceability with the business needs on both sides. We prefer to avoid accepting New York governing law as a general rule, but if Novatek insists we can accept it as long as the injunctive carve-out remains explicit.

Proposed clause (redline-ready):

"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the parties agree that any dispute seeking temporary injunctive relief, a temporary restraining order, or other provisional remedies to prevent irreparable harm shall not be subject to arbitration and either party may seek such relief in the state or federal courts located in the county of the defendant's principal place of business. All other disputes shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration conducted under the rules of the American Arbitration Association (commercial rules). The arbitrator shall apply the substantive law agreed by the parties in the applicable Governing Law clause."

If Novatek requires New York governing law, we recommend adding: "The Governing Law of this Agreement shall be the laws of the State of New York, excluding its choice-of-law rules, provided that the arbitration shall take place in a mutually agreed location or, failing agreement, in Seattle, WA. Injunctive and provisional remedies are preserved as above."

Negotiation strategy:
- Offer: Washington governing law; arbitration in Seattle; injunctive carve-out to local courts.
- Concession: Accept New York governing law only if the arbitration seat defaults to Seattle (or mutually agreed neutral location) and the injunctive carve-out remains intact.

Marcus — please prepare a redline with the exact text above and a short comment explaining why we keep the seat neutral. Jasmine — if Anna confirms Novatek needs NY law as a hard requirement, we can present the concession and rationale.

Vivek Kulkarni
General Counsel (interim), Redwood Inference
